observed: Real photo (scikit-image 'rocket': SpaceX's DSCOVR launch, Falcon 9 on SLC-40, released by SpaceX into the public domain): a white Falcon 9 standing on its launch mount at dusk
Two lightning towers flank the rocket: tapered square steel lattices with X-bracing, a platform on top and a slender mast above it
Two larger lattice towers are cut off at the image edges
A dark transporter-erector strongback shows at the rocket's edges; the launch mount is a light block at the bottom
The camera is level with the pad and far away: verticals stay vertical
inferred: Scale from the rocket's published height (68.4 m) over image rows 127-405: 246 mm/px
Tower geometry measured with that scale: base 8.6 m, platform 3.7 m wide at 54 m, mast to 70 m, axes 32 m either side of the rocket
Towers are assumed to stand in the rocket's plane (their real distances differ)
unknowns: depth of every object (single front view)

evidence.source: published Falcon 9 v1.1 figures: 68.4 m tall, 3.66 m core, 5.2 m fairing
leg lines and platform/mast rows read on 4x zooms of each tower
